resources.string: When an external display is connected
Connected to %1$s. Tap to use your phone as a touchpad
External display connected. Tap to use your phone as a touchpad
Douhua service isn\'t running: tap here to start it on the phone (or run tools/start-server.sh on your computer)
Service version %1$d doesn\'t match app version %2$d: tap here to restart the service (or run tools/stop-server.sh, then tools/start-server.sh)
Douhua service isn\'t responding: tap here to restart it (or run tools/start-server.sh on your computer)
The Douhua service is in use by another connection (another Douhua window or a test tool); it will connect once that one is gone
No DeX display found: keys go to the focused window
The app stopped responding, so the touchscreen was returned to the system
Drag the edges to resize, drag the middle to move
Type with the phone keyboard, tap Send to paste into DeX
Fine control (slow movements move the pointer less, for precise aiming)
Tap, then touch and move = drag
Drag wait time (ms; longer makes dragging easier but clicks slower)
Touch and hold = press left button (after the buzz, move to drag)
Slide along the left/right edge = vertical scroll
Slide along the top/bottom edge = horizontal scroll
Side buttons (top to bottom; Exit and Settings at the top and Hide at the bottom are fixed)
Hide the side buttons (small buttons go in the touchpad corners)
Touchpad corner buttons (when side buttons are hidden; ☰ at bottom left is fixed)
Text on the button (leave empty to use the combo name)
Paste text (type or dictate with the phone keyboard)
Middle click (opens links in a new tab)
DeX: control this phone\'s external display (needs the service started from a computer)
Bluetooth: act as a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse for a computer, tablet or TV (no service needed)
+ Pair a new device (make this phone discoverable)

Tap the line above, then add a device in the computer / tablet / TV Bluetooth settings and pick this phone; keep Douhua open while pairing. If they were paired before, remove the pairing on both sides first, or the other device won\'t see the keyboard and mouse. After pairing, if it also connected to the phone\'s call or media audio, turn those off in the system Bluetooth settings, or the keyboard and mouse will stutter.

%1$s is also connected to this phone\'s call / media audio, so Bluetooth saves power like a headset and the keyboard and mouse stutter (the cursor keeps moving after you stop). Tap here to open the system Bluetooth settings and turn off call and media audio for it (the system may then show it as disconnected; Douhua still works).
No \"Nearby devices\" permission: allow it under Settings → Connection
Bluetooth is off; Douhua will continue when you turn it on
This phone can\'t act as a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse
Waiting: connect to this phone from the other device\'s Bluetooth settings, or pick one in Settings
Bluetooth didn\'t start: another app may be acting as a Bluetooth keyboard; close it and reopen Douhua
System Bluetooth isn\'t responding (this can happen after turning Bluetooth off and on while Douhua is open). Restart the phone to fix it
Text pasting isn\'t available over Bluetooth: the clipboard stays on the phone
This key isn\'t available over Bluetooth
Gentle hum while dragging (reminds you the left button is held)
Grainy feel while moving the pointer (a very faint vibration, like touching a slightly rough surface)
Air mouse page (big buttons: hold to move, left, right…; Bluetooth mode only)
Hold to move (the pointer follows the phone while held; Bluetooth mode only)
Hold to drag (left button down, pointer follows the phone while held; Bluetooth mode only)
Center (pointer to the middle of the screen in one step)
Air mouse only works in Bluetooth mode
This phone has no gyroscope, so air mouse isn\'t available
Air mouse sensitivity (how far the pointer moves for the same turn)
How turning the phone maps to left/right and up/down
Player space (default): up/down = the phone\'s own nod; left/right = turning around vertical (GyroWiki / JoyShockMapper)
Mixed: left/right = turning around vertical; up/down = the phone\'s own nod, with leaning cancelled
World space: left/right = turning around vertical; up/down = nodding around the horizontal axis
Smoothing when still: cutoff (lower = steadier but laggier)
Follow when moving fast: β (higher = keeps up better, but shakier)
How quickly \"moving\" is detected (lower = hand shake is less likely to count as moving, but starts slower)
Soft dead zone: slower than this is scaled down (higher = steadier when holding still, harder to fine-tune)
Path smoothing: sideways wobble along the path is smoothed, forward motion isn\'t delayed (higher = straighter and smoother, corners rounder; 0 = off)
Steady radius: hand wobble within this angle doesn\'t move the pointer (higher = steadier when still; reversing needs a bit more turn; 0 = off)
Center jumps straight to the middle of the screen (absolute position). Devices paired before this version must remove this phone in their Bluetooth settings and pair again once.
Screen shape of %1$s (in the air mouse page, up/down speed depends on it; if wrong, up/down feels faster or slower than left/right)
Vertical line angle correction (if vertical lines lean right at the top, increase)
Horizontal line angle correction (if horizontal lines sink on the right, increase)
Air mouse page buttons (top to bottom, two per row; the round button in the middle is fixed: hold = move, tap = lock moving, tap again = unlock)
\"None\" leaves the key alone. A key with an action belongs to Douhua entirely and no longer changes the volume. \"Hold to move\" on a tap: tap to start, tap again to stop.

Needs the Douhua service running in DeX mode; nothing is taken during calls or while ringing. The service never takes a volume key that shares a device with the power key: on phones where volume down does, only volume up can have an action in DeX mode.
This phone\'s %1$s can\'t be taken on its own (see the service log / Server keys for why), so its action won\'t work
The service can\'t inject keys, so volume keys aren\'t taken (they would stop working)
Couldn\'t find an input device for %1$s on this phone, so its action won\'t work
Couldn\'t take %1$s, so its action won\'t work: %2$s
%1$s can\'t be taken, so their actions won\'t work: %2$s

The service takes over the touchscreen and creates the virtual mouse and keyboard (required in DeX mode; in Bluetooth mode it also blocks system gestures). It has to run as the shell user. Douhua can start it by itself through Wireless debugging, no computer needed. Get every item below ticked.
Wireless debugging only works while the phone is connected to Wi-Fi (mobile data alone or the phone\'s own hotspot won\'t do). No internet needed: being on a router is enough.
Samsung: Settings → About phone → Software information → tap \"Build number\" 7 times. Most other phones: About phone → tap \"Build number\" 7 times.
Turn on \"USB debugging\" in Developer options. No cable needed, but the service lives on it: turning it off stops the service.
Turn on Developer options above first.
Off is fine: Douhua turns it on when starting the service and off again right after (it leaves it alone if you turned it on yourself).

Turn it on in Developer options before starting the service. The first time on a Wi-Fi network the system asks: on your home or another trusted Wi-Fi choose \"Always allow on this network\"; don\'t choose it on public networks. After the first successful start Douhua can turn it on and off by itself.

Wireless debugging is on: devices on the same network can see it. Turn it off when no computer needs to connect to the phone, especially on public networks. Once the service is running, turning it off doesn\'t stop the service (as long as USB debugging stays on).
Only needed once (again after reinstalling Douhua). Steps below.
Tick Wi-Fi, Developer options and USB debugging above first.
The system revoked Douhua\'s key (keys unused for 7 days expire, and revoking USB debugging authorizations clears them). Pair once more.
Follow the steps below; enter the code in Douhua\'s notification. Notification gone? Tap \"Cancel pairing\" and start again.
Douhua\'s notifications are off. The pairing code is entered in a Douhua notification, so allow notifications first (tap here).
1. Turn on Developer options and USB debugging (see above).
2. Tap \"Start pairing\" above: Douhua posts a notification and opens Developer options.

3. Turn on \"Wireless debugging\" (the first time on this Wi-Fi the system asks: choose \"Always allow\" only on your home or another trusted Wi-Fi, see below), tap it to open it, then tap \"Pair device with pairing code\".

4. When the system shows a 6-digit code, pull down the notification shade from the top of the screen, tap \"Enter pairing code\" in Douhua\'s notification, type the code and send. Don\'t leave the system\'s pairing window: it closes as soon as you leave.
5. After pairing, Douhua starts the service by itself; the notification tells you how it went.

Choose \"Always allow\" only on your home Wi-Fi or another network you trust, never on public networks such as cafés, offices or hotels. On a network you always allow, Douhua will later turn Wireless debugging on for a few seconds whenever it starts the service, and during those seconds devices on the same network can see it\'s on. Connecting still needs a paired key or a pairing code, but a flaw that let attackers bypass this check was only fixed in May 2026 (CVE-2026-0073), so don\'t choose it on public networks.
Tap below once the items above are ticked.

The system turned Wireless debugging off again, most likely because this Wi-Fi isn\'t trusted yet. If it\'s your home or another trusted Wi-Fi, open Wireless debugging and choose \"Always allow on this network\" (tap here); not on public networks (see below). If you allow it within 3 minutes, Douhua continues starting the service.
When Douhua opens and the service isn\'t running (or Douhua was just updated), start it; after a reboot, start it once Wi-Fi connects. Turned on after pairing.

Automatic start is paused: when the system asked \"Allow wireless debugging on this network?\", it wasn\'t allowed (maybe a public network). Douhua can\'t see which Wi-Fi it\'s on, so it no longer turns Wireless debugging on by itself, to avoid prompts everywhere; if Wireless debugging is already on, automatic start still works. Tap \"Start service\" above (\"Restart service\" while it\'s running); once that succeeds, automatic start resumes.

Note: turning off USB debugging or Developer options stops the service immediately. Samsung\'s Auto Blocker (Settings → Security and privacy → Auto Blocker) turns USB debugging off; turn Auto Blocker off while using the Douhua service.
Developer options or USB debugging is off
Wireless debugging is off: turn it on in Developer options first

The system turned Wireless debugging off: this Wi-Fi isn\'t trusted. If it\'s your home or another trusted Wi-Fi, open Wireless debugging and choose \"Always allow\" (not on public networks); if you allow it within 3 minutes, Douhua continues
Couldn\'t find Wireless debugging: check it\'s on and the phone is on Wi-Fi
The system revoked Douhua\'s key: pair again
Couldn\'t read or save the key: try pairing again
The start command ran, but the service didn\'t come up
Waiting for \"Pair device with pairing code\"
In Developer options → Wireless debugging, tap \"Pair device with pairing code\". When the system shows the code, enter it in this notification.
Pull down this notification, tap \"Enter pairing code\" and type the 6 digits the system shows. Don\'t leave the system\'s pairing window.
No code received; enter it again.
Wrong pairing code. If the system\'s pairing window is still open, enter it again; if it closed, tap \"Pair device with pairing code\" again.
From now on Douhua starts the service when you open it (can be turned off in settings).
Wireless debugging is still on: turn it off when no computer needs to connect to the phone, especially on public networks. The service keeps running as long as USB debugging stays on.
Paired, but the service didn\'t start
%1$s. In Douhua settings → Douhua service, check which item isn\'t ticked, then tap \"Start service\".
Pairing stopped: it took too long
